THE RULING'S ORDERING FOR THIS RECORD IS OVERTURNED BY THE TREE. It is carried there as "ordered after nothing; it has no caller". RULING: specs/decisions/slice-command-one-path-to-review.md. Read the sections named below before researching; they are cited by heading so they can be found after any renumbering. Figures in this description were measured on 2026-11-24 against the source store and are to be re-measured by this record's own research, not carried.

=== WHAT THIS RECORD OWNS: NARROW THE MILESTONE HANDOFF TO PRINT /slice ===

"One survivor, and what is deleted", row 3, and "Successors", row 4. THIS IS A NEW RECORD THAT REVERSES A CLOSED DELIVERABLE. The ruling assigned this work to handoff_prints_review_stack, revised; that record instead closed as written and is terminal, so its deliverable is now live in the tree and is what this record undoes. Expect a backlog-audit match against it; the match is the reversal, not a duplicate.

WHAT THE HANDOFF DOES TODAY (scripts/milestone-review-handoff.sh, 366 lines; suite 399 lines). It writes review.state and review.ref on the milestone entry, calls review-stack-prepare.sh (`cut`, then `show`), and on the refusal arm prints `/please push <integration branch>` lines and a line about the grant binding to HEAD.

WHAT IT DOES AFTER THIS RECORD. It still detects a finished milestone once and drafts the review summary. It prints one line, `/slice`, and no push line and no merge line. It no longer calls review-stack-prepare.sh, so both arms that hang off that call go, with their cases. It stops writing review.ref; review.state stays as its own fired-once marker and means nothing about slices. It never pushes and never calls a forge, as now.

FILES BEYOND THE RULING'S ROW. review.ref is named in seven files: context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md, context/formats/roadmap-entry-template.md, context/formats/roadmap-format.md, context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md, the handoff, its suite, and scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh. Case H of that last suite asserts the handoff's refusal arm (it was retargeted there by case_h_assertion_review_stack_refusal_arm) and is retargeted again, to the one-line /slice output. scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh names none of these and needs no edit. The git-workflow-narrative.md mention is left to delete_review_stack_inference_route, which rewrites that passage and is ordered after this record; say so in the plan rather than editing it twice.

=== TERRITORY ===

scripts/milestone-review-handoff.sh; scripts/tests/test-milestone-review-handoff.sh; scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh; context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md; context/formats/roadmap-format.md; context/formats/roadmap-entry-template.md; index-entries.json for the line-count reconciliation. Ordered after slice_command_build, so the line it prints names a command that exists, and after slice_bar_measurement_and_declaration for territory only (both reconcile index-entries.json; the edge may be reversed with no other change). delete_review_stack_inference_route and remove_merge_command are ordered after this record.

=== VERIFY BY ===

Both suites green; a search of the handoff for review-stack-prepare, review.ref, `/please push` and the old merge command returning nothing; review.state still written exactly once per finished milestone; generate-context-line-counts.sh --check clean; deploy-headless.sh reporting a clean verify.

RULING: specs/decisions/slice-command-one-path-to-review.md. Read the sections named below before researching; they are cited by heading so they can be found after any renumbering. Figures in this description were measured on 2026-11-24 against the source store and are to be re-measured by this record's own research, not carried.

=== WHAT THIS RECORD OWNS: BAR MEASUREMENT AND THE slice_bar DECLARATION ===

"The size bar" and "Successors", row 2. slice_command_build ships only the default bar. This record adds the other two sources, in the ruling's order: (1) a declared `slice_bar` object, `{lines, files}`, in .claude-extensions.json; (2) otherwise the 75th percentile, nearest-rank, of added lines and of changed files over merged pull requests on the chosen target, when there are at least five; (3) otherwise the shipped default, printed as `default, unmeasured`. The bar line names its source and, when measured, its n. A bar replaced at prompt 2 is recorded as `chosen at prompt`.

WHERE THE MEASUREMENT LIVES. The script contains no forge invocation ("Constraints held"), and merged pull requests are a forge fact. Settle in research whether the population is read by the command file and handed to the script, or derived from history without a forge call; do not put a forge call in the script. The median is rejected by the ruling and is not offered.

WHAT IS COUNTED. Added lines over the slice's paths (the first numstat column of the difference between target and work ref) and the number of paths. Paths declared generated are excluded from the line count and still listed. That declaration is owned by branch_aware_orchestration_and_squash_landing; UNTIL IT EXISTS EVERY PATH COUNTS AND PROMPT 2 SAYS SO. This record is buildable and correct as specified without it: the ruling's edge is from the accuracy of the bar onto that record, not from the bar's existence, so that record is ordered after this one and wires its declaration into the count this record builds. Leave a single, named place in the count where an exclusion list is read.

THE DECLARATION DOCUMENT. Add a `slice_bar` section to context/standards/repo-level-declarations.md. delete_review_stack_inference_route removes the `review_base` section of the same document and is ordered after this record. No number appears in any deliverable as a property of the system: the measured figures in the ruling's E5 are evidence about three repositories and are not copied.

Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout 600000 -- context/patterns/external-process-wait.md Rule 1). No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**. RULING: specs/decisions/slice-command-one-path-to-review.md. Read the sections named below before researching; they are cited by heading so they can be found after any renumbering. Figures in this description were measured on 2026-11-24 against the source store and are to be re-measured by this record's own research, not carried.

=== WHAT THIS RECORD OWNS: BIND A PUSH GRANT TO THE PUSHED REF ===

"Grants", numbered item 1, and "Successors", row 6. Today a grant is matched against `git rev-parse HEAD` at consume time (scripts/lib/push-grant-lib.sh, near line 453; hooks/please-grant.sh records HEAD near line 211) and lives PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW seconds, default 600. For a ref built by plumbing, HEAD is not the commit being pushed. Two consequences the ruling states: (a) any commit by any session inside the window kills the grant although the pushed ref is untouched, which is routine in a repository with live orchestration; (b) the grant does not pin what is pushed, because the ref can be rebuilt between the typed line and the push without the match noticing.

THE CHANGE. A grant for a ref other than the checked-out branch binds to that ref's commit at mint time and is matched against that ref's commit at consume time, instead of HEAD. A grant for the checked-out branch keeps its present behaviour. `/please push <remote> <branch>` already names any branch, checked out or not (hooks/please-grant.sh); this record changes what such a grant is bound to, not who can mint one. One grant at a time, the expiry window and the default-branch force bar are unchanged.

NOT THIS RECORD'S. Items 2 and 3 of "Grants" (a typed `/slice push <id>` minting for a slice ref; a batch grant) are not built here and the ruling does not recommend the third. The `/merge` minting branch of hooks/please-grant.sh is removed by remove_merge_command, which is ordered after this record because both edit that hook; do not touch that branch here.

=== TERRITORY ===

hooks/please-grant.sh; hooks/guard-git-push.sh; scripts/lib/push-grant-lib.sh; scripts/tests/test-please-grant.sh; scripts/tests/test-guard-git-push.sh. Research confirms whether scripts/git-push-granted.sh or any document stating the HEAD binding needs the same change, and extends file_scope if so. Ordered after nothing and independent of /slice; it lowers the cost of slice_command_build's acceptance step in a repository with live orchestration, so it is worth dispatching alongside it.

=== VERIFY BY ===

Suite cases for: a grant for a non-checked-out ref survives an unrelated commit on HEAD inside the window; the same grant is refused once the granted ref itself moves; a grant for the checked-out branch behaves as before; deploy-headless.sh reporting a clean verify. No push is performed by an agent (rules/pr-prohibition.md); every case runs against fixture repositories.

RULING: specs/decisions/slice-command-one-path-to-review.md. Read the sections named below before researching; they are cited by heading so they can be found after any renumbering. Figures in this description were measured on 2026-11-24 against the source store and are to be re-measured by this record's own research, not carried.

=== WHAT THIS RECORD OWNS: THE /slice BUILD ===

Build the one mechanism the ruling keeps ("The ruling in six lines", line 1; "One survivor, and what is deleted", row "new"; "Successors", row 1): a user-invoked command over one small script and one series file. Nothing in the source store names /slice today (commands/slice.md is absent; a search for the command name and for slice_bar returns no file).

THE SCRIPT ("The mechanism"). Three subcommands and no other entry point: check, build, status. check: the target is an ancestor of the work ref; every path in the difference is in exactly one slice or on not_landing; no glob matches nothing; depends_on names real slices and has no cycle; every slice is at or under the bar or carries a reason. build: private index, base tree, overlay of the slice's paths at the work ref, write-tree, commit-tree, compare-and-swap move of refs/heads/slice/<series>/<id>, with HEAD, the index and the working tree untouched; a slice with two or more unmerged dependencies waits, so no slice commit has two parents; build refuses whatever check refuses. status: local ref and remote ref against the recorded commit, and the content-based merged test. No inference code is written: no union-find, no topological sort, no overlap analysis. The script contains no push, checkout, merge or forge invocation, and its suite asserts that statically ("Basis", carried from builder A; "Constraints held").

THE SERIES FILE ("The mechanism"). specs/.orchestration/slices/<series id>.json is the single home of slice state, with the fields that section lists, and the pull-request body beside it as <series id>/<slice id>.md. It is a runtime file: decide in the plan whether context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md gains a row for it, and if so add that file to this record's territory.

THE COMMAND FILE ("The command surface"). commands/slice.md owns what a script must not: resolution, prompt 1 (the target, each candidate shown with its measured difference; a non-ancestor candidate shown and not choosable; an empty difference shown as nothing to slice), the bar line, prompt 2 (the proposal table and its four fixed lines; approve / revise / cancel; nothing written before approve), the per-slice typed push lines printed on approval, the continue step of a later invocation, and the open step (the forge call lives here and nowhere else). User-invoked only, in the same class as /tag. "Re-derive, never rebase": no restack, no three-way merge, no conflict resolution.

THE BAR IN THIS RECORD. Only the shipped default (1,500 lines and 30 files, printed as `default, unmeasured`), the refusal with its two accepted reasons, and the bar being revisable at prompt 2 ("The size bar"). The declared slice_bar key and the measured 75th percentile belong to slice_bar_measurement_and_declaration and are not built here. Every path counts toward the bar and prompt 2 says so.

NOT THIS RECORD'S. Deleting review-stack-prepare.sh (delete_review_stack_inference_route), narrowing the handoff (narrow_handoff_to_print_slice), removing /merge (remove_merge_command), the grant binding (bind_push_grant_to_pushed_ref), and doc parity plus the operator runbook (stack_pr_redeploy_and_second_repo_demo). Do not base the script on review-stack-prepare.sh ("Basis": no existing code is the basis).

=== ACCEPTANCE IS NOT A SUITE COUNT ===

"Successors", closing paragraph, and "Risks", first item: this record ends with one real slice of a real difference, pushed by a typed grant and opened as a pull request by the operator typing /slice. Two builders with green suites and no pull request are what the ruling deletes. An agent can neither push nor open a pull request (rules/pr-prohibition.md), so the IMPLEMENTING AGENT STOPS SHORT: it builds, tests, redeploys, and returns with the record NOT closed, naming the exact lines the operator types. The record closes only after the operator has pushed one slice and opened its pull request with /slice, and the request URL is recorded in the series file. remove_merge_command reads that as its precondition. A real difference exists to cut: this repository's work branch is several hundred commits ahead of its remote default branch.

=== TERRITORY ===

New commands/slice.md; one new script and its suite (filenames are settled by the plan; add them to file_scope then); manifest.json and scripts/tests/suite-classification.data rows for the three new files. Ordered after nothing. Dispatchable alongside bind_push_grant_to_pushed_ref, with which it shares no file.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

Repo-agnostic: no branch name, remote name or consumer path in any deliverable; the target, the remote and the bar are resolved or chosen at run time. No number appears in a deliverable as a property of the system beyond the default labelled unmeasured. The commit-containment scripts are not edited and not depended on; completed tasks' modified_files is a grouping hint only.

=== VERIFY BY ===

The suite green, including the static no-push / no-forge assertion and a union check (target tree overlaid with every slice equals the work ref's tree on every assigned path); deploy-headless.sh reporting a clean verify; then, by the operator, one slice pushed by a typed grant and opened by /slice, its URL recorded.

### 696. Narrow batch gate stage verify deploy invocation
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Narrow the orchestration batch-gate stage's own verify-deploy invocation: gate the stage on modified_files, honor the gate cache, and bound its wall clock

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-batch-gate.sh (never the deployed .claude/** mirror, which is a gitignored disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/**.

MEASURED, this repository, 2026-11-23, session sess_1795478339_253676: a single-task /orchestrate batch whose implement phase modified exactly three markdown files under specs/decisions/ and nothing else. The batch gate stage ran roughly 45 minutes of wall clock and returned two confirmed findings, BOTH unattributed to the task (pre-existing failures in tests/test-gate-lock.sh and tests/test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh); the attributed set was empty. Zero task-caused findings. The task had already reached completed and committed before the stage started, the stage being advisory by contract.

FOUR COMPOUNDING CAUSES, each independently checkable.

1. The trigger predicate reads the wrong field. orchestrate-batch-gate.sh fires whenever the multi-state .implement_agents map is non-empty -- whenever ANY implement dispatch occurred -- and never consults what that dispatch touched. The information needed sits in the same file: .invocation_modified_files. The per-task postflight already computes exactly this predicate and reported "[deploy-check] modified_files do not overlap agent-system/extensions/** -- not applicable, passing through" roughly 45 minutes before the stage swept that tree anyway.

2. The invocation declines every narrowing verify-deploy.sh offers. The call is: verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet <root> --override-batch-gate-deferral. No --skip-slow, no --skip-unchanged, no --gate8-touched. The script's own comment states the full depth is deliberate ("Capture: full depth (no --skip-slow), explicit TARGET, exactly once"), so this is a design choice to revisit explicitly, not an oversight to patch silently.

3. No cache reuse, although the run was cache-eligible. verify-deploy.sh's --skip-unchanged caching requires no --only-gate, no --gate8-touched, non-nested and non-stale -- all true of this call. It is simply not passed, so every invocation recomputes the whole battery cold even when nothing under agent-system/** or .claude/** is dirty (git status over those paths was empty for this run).

4. No timeout anywhere in orchestrate-batch-gate.sh (grep: zero hits), while skill-orchestrate's bounded-wait idiom for it is a 540-second kill-0 loop. Gate 31's slow cost-class bucket is serialized and, per tests/suite-cost-hints.txt, the nine selected suites sum to roughly 18 minutes (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh alone 543000 ms; test-verify-deploy-gate-selection-crash-net.sh 148607 ms; test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh 106551 ms). Three of the nine are verify-deploy's own self-tests, each booting a complete nested verify-deploy run inside a /tmp fixture -- observed as a four-level-deep process tree. An 18-minute floor against a 540-second wait window GUARANTEES at least three wait rounds per invocation. The recurrence is arithmetic, not a hang, which is why it reproduces every run rather than intermittently.

REMEDY TO DESIGN, in rising cost. Decide between these explicitly and record the rejected alternatives; do not apply all four by reflex.
  (a) No-op the stage when no task's own invocation_modified_files intersects the deploy tree (agent-system/** or .claude/**), reusing the predicate the per-task deploy-check already applies rather than authoring a second one. Cheapest, and it alone would have reduced this run's stage to nothing.
  (b) Pass --skip-unchanged so the existing gate cache is honored.
  (c) Pass --gate8-touched with the batch's union of invocation_modified_files, routing gates 8 and 31 through lib/suite-selection-lib.sh's suite_selection_select; a specs-only batch narrows to the empty set.
  (d) Give the stage a timeout, so a runaway surfaces as a finding instead of as wall clock.

NON-NEGOTIABLE INVARIANT, surviving whichever shape is chosen: the complete gate set still runs once per batch for a batch that DOES touch the deploy tree, deferred and never forgiven. A narrowed or skipped run must never be presented as equivalent to a full-battery pass -- context/contracts/batch-gate-stage.md and verify-deploy.sh's own forced-dirty note both already carry that distinction and must keep agreeing with whatever lands here.

TERRITORY, two adjacent live records. Read both before designing; duplicate neither.
  Task 586 (suite and gate wall-clock cost consumer, status partial) owns the COST half: its declared file_scope already covers tests/suite-cost-hints.txt, tests/test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, tests/run-all.sh, scripts/verify-deploy.sh and scripts/measure-gate-costs.sh, and its subject is deleting, optimizing or demoting the suites the cost probe indicts. The 543-second cache-equivalence suite is exactly such a suite. This record must NOT re-litigate suite cost; the measurement above is fresh evidence for 586, and a serializing dependency edge is owed because the two file scopes overlap on verify-deploy.sh.
  Task 599 (batch-gate-deferral narrowing form, status not_started) owns a DIFFERENT surface: the "## Batch Gate Deferral" directive composed by scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, which tells a dispatched implement agent what narrowing to run when the gate defers. That is dispatch-time guidance to an agent; this record is the close-time invocation the stage makes itself. Keep the two distinct, and make whatever repository-level declaration surface 599 chooses for narrowing forms serve this record too rather than standing up a second declaration.

VERIFICATION. Extend scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-batch-gate.sh (or create it if absent) with a specs-only-batch case asserting the stage no-ops, and a deploy-tree-touching case asserting the full battery still runs once. Per the baseline-relative criterion rule, state the acceptance criterion against this repository's standing pre-existing findings rather than against an absolute clean gate: tests/test-gate-lock.sh and tests/test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh are currently red for unrelated reasons and must not be read as this record's regressions.

### 695. Design the /slice command: one clean path from work branch to a stack of review pull requests
- **Status**: [COMPLETED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: None
- **Research**: [695_slice_command_design_and_consolidation/reports/01_slice-command-design.md]
- **Plan**: [695_slice_command_design_and_consolidation/plans/01_slice-command-design.md]
- **Summary**: [695_slice_command_design_and_consolidation/summaries/01_slice-command-design-summary.md]

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout 600000 -- context/patterns/external-process-wait.md Rule 1). No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

=== THIS IS A RESEARCH-AND-RULE RECORD, AND ITS MANDATE IS EXPLICITLY REVISIONARY ===

Operator direction, 2026-11-23, verbatim in substance: "I don't want to assume that what is built is already right or worth keeping, or that what is planned is the best way to go." Treat NOTHING below as settled, INCLUDING the two decision records this repository has already accepted. The deliverable is the simplest design that actually works, not a reconciliation that preserves existing investment.

The target is ONE clean and clear method for moving changes from a work branch into a stack of pull requests on an integration branch or branches as appropriate, driven by a `/slice` command. Removing capability is an expected and welcome outcome, not a cost to be minimised.

=== THE COMMAND SURFACE THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR ===

`/slice [description]`. The description is OPTIONAL. When it is absent the command asks the user to select the integration branch the pull request is to be submitted to for review. That selection prompt is part of the design: decide whether the branch set is read from declarations, from remotes, from open pull requests, or offered as a free choice, and whether "or branches as appropriate" means one invocation can target more than one.

Design the command, not just the plumbing. State what `/slice` shows, what it asks, in what order, and what a user who types it with no argument and no prior setup sees. The approval prompt is the product.

=== THE DECISIVE FINDING THIS RESEARCH MUST START FROM ===

TWO INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATIONS OF SUBSTANTIALLY THE SAME THING EXIST. One is in the agent system and has never opened a pull request. The other is in a consumer repository and has opened 22, of which 18 merged.

  A. `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/review-stack-prepare.sh`, 1,572 lines, suite `scripts/tests/test-review-stack-prepare.sh` at 61 passing cases. Subcommands `cut`, `show`, `record-request`, `restack`. Derives review units RETROACTIVELY from landing proofs: union-find over dependency edges and proof path overlap, topological order with ancestry tie-breaks, overlay on `merge-base(review_base, integration_branch)`, moved-base three-way `merge-tree` recompute, compare-and-swap ref moves. Zero pull requests opened with it.

  B. `/home/benjamin/Projects/Sapience/sf1-engine/integration/tools/build-pr-slices.sh`, 2,165 lines, with the path-cut slice table at `vision/pr-series.md` (418 lines) and the ruling at `vision/decisions/pr-release-pipeline.md` (518 lines). Slices are PATH-CUT from a hand-maintained table with a measured size ceiling. 22 pull requests opened, 18 merged, per `gh api` evidence recorded in that record under RP3.

READ B BEFORE DESIGNING ANYTHING. It is prior art the operator already owns, it is the only one of the two with production evidence, and its own section 8 ("Successors") already files "Upstream requirements ... in the agent-system source-store repository, not here" -- meaning it expects this repository to receive requirements from it. Its section 4 table states precisely which agent-system mechanisms it waits on and which it does not use.

THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS, TO BE TESTED AND NOT ASSUMED: B should be promoted upstream into the agent system as the basis for `/slice`, and A's inference machinery should be deleted rather than finished. Test it. B is 2,165 lines in a consumer repo with repo-specific assumptions baked in, and promoting it may cost more than it saves. Reach a verdict with reasons either way.

=== THE CONTRADICTION THAT MUST BE SETTLED ===

The two accepted records disagree on whether a review base exists.

  - `specs/decisions/review-slices-are-declared-tasks.md` (this repository), S3: affirms `review_base` as a branch distinct from `integration_branch`, and keeps the existing refusal when they are equal.
  - sf1-engine's RP1: "The declared branch is the integration branch, and there is no review base." An independent slice is based on `origin/main`; a dependent slice on the slices it depends on. Its rejected-alternative paragraph says a review base "protects against nothing here: `main` already contains everything a slice is based on."

RP1 carries measured evidence; S3 does not. S3 was written in the same session that created this record and is the weaker of the two. If the research concludes RP1 is right, SAY SO and amend S3 -- do not preserve it out of deference. The whole of `review-slices-are-declared-tasks.md` is in scope for amendment, including its retention list.

=== THE MEASURED BAR THE AGENT SYSTEM LACKS ENTIRELY ===

sf1-engine RP3 sets a slice ceiling from what has actually merged: at most 1,500 hand-written changed lines and 30 files for backlog slices; 3,000 lines or 30 files before a milestone divides into stacked parts; generated and mechanical files excluded from the count and verified by a command. Median over 18 merged pull requests: 10 files, 1,258 added lines.

The agent system has NO size bar. A slice nobody can review is the failure mode the whole pipeline exists to prevent, so this is the single clearest piece of value to promote upstream. Decide whether the bar is a declaration, a default with a per-repository override, or a refusal, and whether the numbers are portable or must be re-measured per repository.

=== REMOVAL IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE: FOUR OVERLAPPING MECHANISMS, ONE SURVIVOR ===

Enumerate every path that currently moves work toward review, rule which single one survives, and state what happens to each of the others. Known today:

  1. `scripts/milestone-ref-land.sh` -- retired as a landing mechanism and fully unwired in the source store; its deletion is owned by the record named `milestone_ref_land_recreates_retired_ref`.
  2. `scripts/review-stack-prepare.sh` -- mechanism A above.
  3. `scripts/milestone-review-handoff.sh` -- prints per-task listings and the operator commands.
  4. `commands/merge.md` single-branch mode, plus the stack mode authored by `merge_command_stack_mode`.
  5. sf1-engine's `build-pr-slices.sh` -- mechanism B, currently outside the agent system.

Also rule on the `/merge` single-branch mode itself. Every record so far has declared its defects a non-goal: it acts on the checked-out branch, refuses outright on main or master, and hardcodes the remote `origin` and the target `main`. That is why the handoff record must SUPPRESS a printed `/merge` rather than print a working one. "One clean and clear method" means fixing it or removing it, not routing around it indefinitely.

=== CONSTRAINTS THAT DO NOT BEND ===

- `rules/pr-prohibition.md`: no agent-reachable path pushes or opens a pull request. Every push stays behind a typed `/please`; every forge call stays inside a user-invoked command. A design that needs an agent to push is out of bounds, not a trade-off.
- Repo-agnostic: no literal branch name, remote name or consumer-repo path in any deliverable landing under `agent-system/**`. sf1-engine is EVIDENCE, never a hardcoded assumption.
- The grant cost is real and must be stated, not designed around: an N-slice stack costs N typed `/please push` grants, each bound to HEAD when typed inside a 600-second window, dying when any session commits in between. If the design implies a batch grant, say so and name it as separate work rather than assuming it.

=== OPEN RECORDS THIS MUST REACH A VERDICT ON, NOT SILENTLY ORPHAN ===

For each, state: survives unchanged, survives revised, or should be abandoned.

  - `handoff_prints_review_stack` [planned] -- handoff printing the stack.
  - `merge_command_stack_mode` [planned] -- `/merge --stack`.
  - `stack_pr_redeploy_and_second_repo_demo` [not_started] -- now doc parity, redeploy and the operator runbook.
  - `milestone_ref_land_recreates_retired_ref` [not_started] -- deletion of the retired script.
  - `branch_aware_orchestration_and_squash_landing` [not_started] -- the generated-file collapse declaration, which makes a slice diff readable.
  - The five HELD worktree and two-root records (`two_root_contract_dispatch_and_commit_scripts`, `two_root_contract_in_hooks`, `two_root_classification_of_remaining_consumers`, `batch_worktree_cleanup_retention_orphan_report`, `batch_worktree_creation_when_isolation_on`). sf1-engine RP7 rules isolation off and lists an isolation spike as a successor. Say whether declared slices make isolation attractive, irrelevant, or abandonable.

OUT OF SCOPE, AND DELIBERATELY SO: the commit-containment cluster on `scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh` and `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` (six open records plus two more). It is the substrate slicing sits on, it is heavily contended territory, and widening into it would make this record undispatchable. Name any dependency on it as an edge; do not edit it.

=== DELIVERABLE ===

A research report, then a decision record under `specs/decisions/` that rules the `/slice` design and supersedes or amends `review-slices-are-declared-tasks.md` as the findings require. The record states: the command surface; which of the two implementations is the basis and what happens to the other; whether a review base exists; the slice size bar and its portability; which of the four existing mechanisms survive and what is deleted; and a verdict row for every open record listed above.

No implementation in this record. It researches and rules; successors build.

=== VERIFY BY ===

Every claim about either implementation re-derived from the live files, with line numbers, not carried from this description. A reader can tell from the decision record alone which single mechanism survives and which files are to be deleted. Every record in the verdict list has a stated disposition. The report names at least one thing that was built or planned and is now to be discarded -- if it names none, the revisionary mandate above was not exercised.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel c, follow-up task) of an /orchestrate invocation over three tasks, session sess_1795451386_ec8465. User-approved at the lead level.

THE GAP: nothing in admission or pre-dispatch review observes that a plan's phase count exceeds what one implement dispatch can plausibly close. A plan is admitted on artifact existence alone, so an under-decomposed task is discovered only after the run is underway -- by which point the operator has already paid for the dispatches that revealed it.

MEASURED IMPACT: in the originating invocation a seven-phase plan was admitted as a single task. Its first implement dispatch ran roughly 30 minutes and 127 tool calls to close phase 1 alone and returned status=partial at 1/7; a second continuation dispatch ran roughly 26 minutes and 91 tool calls to close phase 2 and returned partial at 2/7. The remaining five phases are each comparable in size, so the task as filed represented several hours of dispatch time across at least five more cycles. The run was closed deliberately at 2/7 rather than continuing, and that judgment had to be made by the operator mid-run with no prior signal.

WHY PRE-DISPATCH REVIEW IS THE SITE: scripts/orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh already runs once per invocation before any dispatch, already carries nine advisory defect classes (dependency-edge classification, metadata defects, self-modification, missing serializing edges, session contention, absent-scope, cross-session hazard, dirty worktree, file_scope shape), and is already advisory-loud rather than blocking. A phase-count signal is the same shape as what it already emits and needs no new invocation site.

DELIVERABLE: add an advisory class that reads each admitted candidate's newest plan artifact, counts its phase headings, and warns when that count exceeds a declared threshold -- naming the task, the count, and that a split is the remedy. ADVISORY ONLY: it must never block a dispatch, never fail one, never alter a status, and never gate admission. Prefer deriving the threshold from observed close rates where that is cheap; otherwise a single declared constant with its rationale stated at the declaration site is acceptable. Fixture coverage must pin both a plan over the threshold (warns) and one under it (silent), and must assert that the warning changes no exit code.

SEPARATE, NOT INCLUDED HERE: dividing the specific seven-phase task that motivated this record is a task-management operation (/task --expand on that record, which retires it and files its remainder as children) and is the operator's call, not a deliverable of this one. This record owns only the detection signal.

### 688. Dispatch redeploy clears staleness verdict
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: Task 501

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate invocation over three tasks, session sess_1795451386_ec8465. User-approved at the lead level.

THE DEFECT: the completion-deploy gate in postflight refuses an implement dispatch's completion write (exit 6, "extension 'core' is stale relative to its source store") even when the dispatch being completed has ALREADY run deploy-headless.sh itself to a clean result. The staleness signal the gate reads is not refreshed by a deploy performed inside the dispatch, so the redeploy is effectively performed twice and an entire additional orchestration cycle is consumed doing nothing but re-deploying and reconciling.

MEASURED IMPACT: in the originating invocation two of six cycles were spent on this class alone. One task's dispatch closed all three of its phases and passed its scoped verification, then had its completion write refused and waited a full cycle for the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint to promote it. The second occurrence is the sharper one: that dispatch ran deploy-headless.sh as its own terminal phase, landing clean at 41 checks and 0 failures, and postflight STILL refused on a stale-core verdict -- so the work was complete, the deploy was current, and a cycle was burned anyway.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG: the recovery path itself is correct and automatic -- the checkpoint deploys, reconciles, and promotes without operator action, and both affected tasks reached completed status with their plan stamps and state writes intact. The gate is also right to exist: refusing a completion write against a stale deployed tree is the behaviour that keeps a deploy artifact from being trusted when it diverges from its source. The defect is narrowly that the gate cannot observe a deploy that happened inside the dispatch it is gating.

DELIVERABLE: make a dispatch-performed deploy observable to the postflight completion-deploy gate, so a dispatch that leaves the tree current is not refused. Either re-probe freshness at gate time rather than reading a verdict computed earlier in the cycle, or have deploy-headless.sh record a landing the gate can read and compare against the dispatch window. The gate MUST still refuse when the tree is genuinely stale; this is a freshness-observation fix, never a relaxation of the gate's criterion. Fixture coverage must pin both directions explicitly: a dispatch that deployed is admitted, and a dispatch that did not deploy against a stale tree is still refused with exit 6.

TERRITORY: file_scope overlaps the open record cycle_postflight_containment_parity at scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh. That record owns a different defect in the same file (containment parity in what a cycle commit stages) and the two must not be worked concurrently; a dependencies[] edge is declared so they serialise rather than collide.

CITATIONS -- issue-log entries this record is built from:
  {task 486, iss_1795458111817_E2ou8C} -- class "stale deploy or source-store boundary", severity costly, implement phase. First occurrence.
  {task 675, iss_1795458111998_VgGZ4g} -- class "stale deploy or source-store boundary", severity costly, implement phase. Second occurrence, the dispatch that had already deployed.

### 685. Cut review branches and submit a stack of PRs from landed integration-branch work
- **Status**: [EXPANDED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: Task 673, Task 687
- **Research**: [685_stack_pr_submission_from_integration_branch/reports/01_stack-pr-submission.md]
- **Plan**: [685_stack_pr_submission_from_integration_branch/plans/01_stack-pr-submission.md]
- **Handoff**: [685_stack_pr_submission_from_integration_branch/handoffs/phase-3-handoff-20261123T212251Z.md]

**Description**: Cut review branches and submit a stack of PRs from landed integration-branch work

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** in the repository that owns the source store, never a deployed .claude/** tree. Edit the mirrored path, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language under agent-system/**.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The branch-topology work ends at "work is landed on the integration branch" plus a review handoff that prints the commands a human types. Nothing in it cuts a review branch, opens a pull request, chooses a PR's base, or maintains a stack of dependent PRs. That gap is this task. The aim stated by the operator is a workflow that runs off a long-lived feature branch and submits reviewable PRs from it, stacking them where the work is dependent.

THE CONSENT BOUNDARY IS NOT RE-OPENED. rules/pr-prohibition.md and ruling R8 of specs/decisions/branch-topology-and-landing-strategy.md both stand unchanged: an agent never pushes and never creates a PR or MR. This task PREPARES -- it computes branches, bases, ordering and descriptions, and hands the operator the literal commands. Every outward call stays behind the user-invoked /please grant and /merge. hooks/guard-git-push.sh enforces this mechanically regardless of what is built here, so a design that tried to bypass it would simply fail.

PRIOR ART TO READ, NOT REINVENT. The cslib extension's /pr command already implements the three workflows this needs -- a new PR, a PR stacked on another (`--stacked [PR]`: branch from the parent PR's head, `gh pr create --base <pr-head>`), and updating or amending an existing PR. It is the only stacking machinery in the repository. It is also welded to its own repository: a Lean CI pipeline, `lake` invocations throughout, and a hardcoded upstream remote and branch. ASSESS AND RULE whether the portable part -- workflow selection, base resolution, branch naming, PR body composition -- can be extracted into core with the CI pipeline left as an extension-supplied hook, or whether core needs its own smaller implementation. State the reasoning; do not assume either answer.

DEPENDS ON A CONTRACT THE LANDING TASK OWES. The landing task is required to state what a downstream PR-cutting step receives: the ref to branch from, the commit range covered, and whether that range is already one commit per task. Read that contract rather than re-deriving it. If it is absent or ambiguous when this task is planned, that is a blocker to raise, not a gap to fill by guessing.

1. REVIEW UNIT. Rule what one PR contains -- one task, one batch, or an operator-chosen range -- and how its branch is named. The unit must be stated in terms of the landing contract above, not invented here.
2. BASE RESOLUTION. A PR's base is the integration branch for the bottom of a stack, and the parent PR's head branch for every PR above it. Build the resolution, including detecting an existing parent PR rather than requiring the operator to supply its number every time.
3. STACK ORDERING FROM DEPENDENCY EDGES. Tasks already declare `dependencies` in specs/state.json. Rule whether the stack order is derived from those edges, supplied by the operator, or both, and what happens when the edges imply an order the landed commit order contradicts.
4. RE-TARGETING WHEN A PARENT MERGES. This is the part no existing machinery has. When the bottom PR merges, every PR above it needs its base moved and may need rebasing. Rule what is automated, what is prepared-for-the-operator, and what is explicitly out of scope. `git rebase -i` is unavailable; a non-interactive rebase or a plumbing-built equivalent is the only candidate.
5. PREPARED COMMANDS, NEVER EXECUTED. Extend or replace milestone-review-handoff.sh so the handoff names each PR in the stack, in order, with its base, its title, its body, and the literal /please and /merge invocations. One grant per push is the existing contract; if a stack of N PRs means N grants, say so plainly rather than designing around it.
6. PLATFORM. /merge already detects GitHub versus GitLab from the remote. Stacking semantics differ between them. Rule which platforms are supported and refuse loudly on an unsupported one rather than producing a malformed request.
7. SECOND-REPOSITORY USE. The operator's stated purpose is submitting stacks in a repository other than the one owning the source store. Nothing built here may hardcode a repository, a remote name, a branch name or a path. Verify against a second repository, not only the source-store repository.

NON-GOALS: changing the consent boundary; implementing worktree isolation, which is held; re-ruling the landing mechanism, which belongs to the landing task.

VERIFICATION CRITERIA THIS TASK OWNS:
- A stack of at least three dependent PRs is prepared from landed work, each with the correct base, in dependency order, with no agent having pushed or called a forge API.
- The prepared commands, run by the operator, produce the stack on the forge.
- A parent merging produces a stated, tested disposition for its descendants rather than a silently stale base.
- Every deliverable is repo-agnostic, demonstrated in a repository other than the source-store repository.

### 684. Sweep and fix stale command and sub-mode references across the source store
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: core-agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Sweep the source store for slash-command references that name a command or sub-mode that does not exist or does not accept what is named, fix every one, and extend the existing lint so the class cannot silently return.

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/** in /home/benjamin/.config/nvim (resolve via .claude-extensions.json's .extensions.<name>.source_dir). Never hand-author under a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY afterwards via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description.

== THE MOTIVATING DEFECT ==

An operator asked what `/distill --meta` does, after an orchestration conclusion report named it as the consumer of recorded channel (b)/(c) proposals. There is no such sub-mode. extensions/memory/commands/distill.md states plainly, at its own lines 13, 74, 160 and 174, that `--meta`, `--review` and `--dream` MOVED to `/telemetry`; `/distill` accepts only `--auto`, `--revise`, `--learn`. The conclusion stage, the batch-results template and the events format all still tell the reader to run a command that will be rejected as an unknown flag.

This is not one typo. It is the residue of a sub-mode migration that updated the owning command file and left every downstream citation behind.

== WHY THE EXISTING LINT DID NOT CATCH IT ==

scripts/lint/lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh already guards a neighbouring class, and its design is sound: it enumerates valid commands at run time from every */commands/*.md reachable from the extensions root, hardcodes no allowlist, and scans the full corpus including context/ and docs/ prose and embedded JSON example strings. Read its header before touching it -- it already records why it is a separate file rather than an extension of lint-routing-wiring.sh or lint-contract-compliance.sh.

It misses this defect on two independent axes, and BOTH must be closed:

(1) IT VALIDATES THE COMMAND NAME ONLY, NEVER THE FLAG. `/distill` exists, so `/distill --meta` passes. Command existence and sub-mode acceptance are different predicates.

(2) IT MATCHES A RECOMMENDATION SHAPE ONLY (a literal `Next: /X` or `Run /X` line). Every `/distill --meta` occurrence found is ordinary inline prose -- "awaiting the batched, dedup-aware consumer, `/distill --meta`" -- which that shape does not reach.

A NAIVE FLAG CHECK IS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THIS IS THE CENTRAL DESIGN PROBLEM. Grepping the owning command file for the flag string returns a FALSE PASS here: distill.md contains the literal text `--meta` precisely because it documents that the flag moved away. The validator must distinguish a flag the command ACCEPTS from a flag it merely MENTIONS as moved, removed or unavailable. Decide and document how that discrimination is made (an explicit accepted-flag declaration the command files carry, a parse of the documented argument-dispatch block, or a negative-context exclusion), and pin the discrimination with a fixture whose command file mentions a flag only in a moved/removed sentence.

== MEASURED EVIDENCE -- RE-DERIVE, DO NOT TRUST THESE COUNTS ==

Probed 2026-11-22 over agent-system/extensions/ (*.md, *.sh, *.json), matching backticked `/cmd --flag` and bare `/cmd` references. Re-derive every figure before acting; they fix the SHAPE of the work, not its exact contents.

M1. `/distill --meta` -- 7 occurrences, 4 files:
  - core/context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md (3: Step 4b, Step 4c, Step 6's report instruction)
  - core/context/patterns/orchestrate-batch-results-template.md (2: the channel (b) and channel (c) render lines)
  - core/context/formats/events-format.md (1: the conclusion_proposal_recorded row's "Consumed later, in batches, by" clause)
  - books/context/project/books/patterns/books-revise-submode.md (1: "it governs this sub-mode identically")
The correct target in all seven is `/telemetry --meta`. Confirm against distill.md and telemetry.md rather than against this list.

M2. REFERENCES TO A COMMAND WITH NO DEFINITION FILE ANYWHERE. `/zotero --setup` appears in literature/scripts/zotero-chunk.sh:133 and zotero-attach-chunks.sh:100,106 -- inside RUNTIME ERROR MESSAGES printed to the user, which is strictly worse than prose: the operator is told at the moment of failure to run something that does not exist. `/errors --fix N` appears in nvim/context/project/neovim/hooks/wezterm-integration.md:90 and core/hooks/wezterm-task-number.sh:12,65. Determine for each whether the command was removed (fix the reference) or lives outside the scanned extensions root (fix the scan, not the reference) -- do not assume the first.

M3. FLAG NOT FOUND ON THE NAMED COMMAND: `/literature --scan`, `/literature --search`, `/sheet --quick`. These are UNCONFIRMED and at least one is a probe artifact: two different extensions ship a `commands/sheet.md`, and a crude first-match lookup resolved `/sheet` to the wrong one. Treat M3 as a list to adjudicate, not a list to fix. The duplicate-basename case is itself a finding about the validator: a command name resolving to more than one file must be handled deliberately, not by first match.

M4. BARE REFERENCES TO THE REMOVED LIFECYCLE TRIAD: `/implement` (14), `/plan` (13), `/research` (11). The existing lint's own header names these three as the removal that motivated it, so a live RECOMMENDATION of them is already guarded; these 38 survive because they are not in the recommendation shape. Most are expected to be legitimate historical prose. THE SWEEP MUST NOT MECHANICALLY REWRITE THEM. Distinguishing a live instruction to run a dead command from a historical account of its removal is a judgment call, and a validator that cannot make it must report the occurrence rather than rewrite it.

M5. CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVES, for the fixture set: `/tmp`, `/proc`, `/dev` (filesystem paths); `/ide`, `/help` (Claude Code built-ins, not agent-system commands). The validator must not flag these.

== WHAT TO BUILD ==

A. FLAG-LEVEL VALIDATION, extending lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh rather than adding a second lint, unless reading it in full shows the hosts are genuinely incompatible -- in which case state why, in the same register its own NET-SIZE RATIONALE section uses. The run-time enumeration of valid commands is already there and must be reused, never forked. Preserve its no-hardcoded-allowlist property at the flag level too: the accepted-flag set must be derived from the command files themselves, so adding or removing a sub-mode changes the verdict with no edit to the lint.

B. WIDEN THE MATCHED SHAPE from the recommendation line to any backticked command reference, while keeping the false positives in M5 out. The existing lint deliberately scans the full corpus including context/ and docs/; that scope stays.

C. FIX EVERY CONFIRMED OCCURRENCE, M1 first (unambiguous and highest-traffic), then M2 and M3 as adjudicated. Each fix names the command that actually owns the capability.

D. RETIRE THE LINT'S OWN FINDINGS TO ZERO within this landing event, matching the zero-tolerance, no-allowlist posture the existing lint already declares for itself. If a residual occurrence cannot be retired, that is a finding to report, not an allowlist entry to add.

== DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RULE ON DURING PLANNING (do not silently default) ==

Q1. How is "a flag this command accepts" determined, given the false-pass trap above? Argue the options; a solution that requires every command file to gain a new declaration block is a corpus-wide change and must be costed as one.

Q2. What is the verdict on a command name that resolves to more than one commands/*.md file across extensions (the /sheet case in M3)? Both-must-accept, any-may-accept, or report-the-ambiguity-as-its-own-finding.

Q3. Does a reference inside a runtime error message (M2) warrant a stronger verdict than the same reference in prose? It reaches the operator at their least recoverable moment, which is an argument for treating it as a higher severity; against, a second severity tier is machinery this lint does not currently have.

Q4. How does the validator treat a historical mention (M4) without either rewriting it or drowning the report in it? Fix the rule before touching any of the 38.

== CONSTRAINTS ==

- Repo-agnostic: no consumer-repo-specific path or literal in any deliverable.
- The lint's existing verdicts must not regress: whatever it catches today it still catches after.
- An adjacent open task covers the BEHAVIOR of the --meta evidence consumer (its dedup, cap and consolidation channel). This task is reference hygiene only and must not change what --meta does. Their declared file_scopes do not intersect; keep it that way.

Rebase onto whatever those edits became; do not assume the probed line numbers still hold.

3. REMOVAL: `git worktree remove` WITHOUT --force. A refusal is reported and the worktree stays.

5. RETENTION: a task left [PARTIAL], [BLOCKED], failed or abandoned keeps worktree and branch for resume. A batch holding both landed and retained tasks keeps both.
6. /refresh LISTS batch records whose session is not live and whose worktree still exists. It REMOVES NOTHING.

### 673. Land one reviewable commit per completed task on the integration branch and verify it before the status write
- **Status**: [COMPLETED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: Task 669
- **Research**: [673_per_task_attribution_squash_landing/reports/01_isolation-off-landing-ruling.md]
- **Plan**: [673_per_task_attribution_squash_landing/plans/01_landing-verification-gate.md]
- **Summary**: [673_per_task_attribution_squash_landing/summaries/01_landing-verification-gate-summary.md]

**Description**: Land one reviewable commit per completed task on the integration branch and verify it before the status write

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** in the repository that owns the source store, never a deployed .claude/** tree. Edit the mirrored path, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language under agent-system/**.

RULING THIS TASK BUILDS: specs/decisions/batch-worktree-isolation-and-task-squash-landing.md (the amending record), sections "R3, amended", "Defects engaged" entry 4, and "Built-mechanism verdicts" (the retirement). Read them before planning; they are cited, not restated, and the record wins over this description wherever the two differ. Evidence: specs/667_amend_branch_topology_per_batch_worktree_squash/reports/01_batch-worktree-squash-amendment.md.

SCOPE RE-POINTED BY OPERATOR DIRECTION, 2026-11-23. Worktree isolation is deferred and its tasks are on hold. The isolation-off path, which the amending record treated as a constraint the design must also satisfy, is now the ONLY path this task builds and verifies. The two-root prerequisites are held and this task no longer waits on them: it runs in the one primary tree, where there is exactly one root.

=== THE CONTRADICTION THIS TASK MUST RULE BEFORE IT BUILDS ===

The amending record's landing mechanism reads a batch branch: "select the task's own commits on the batch branch between the merge base and the batch tip by the `task {N}` subject convention". Its own standing constraint says every behaviour must hold where "no worktree and no batch branch exist". With isolation off there is no batch branch to read, and the primary tree is already on the integration branch, so a task's phase commits land there directly as they are made. There is therefore nothing to cherry-pick FROM, and one-commit-per-task cannot be produced by picking.

This was survivable while isolation-on was the primary path. It is now the blocking design question, and the research round must rule it rather than inherit it. RULE between at least these, state the reasoning, and record it as a decision record under specs/decisions/:

A. SIDE BRANCH WITHOUT A WORKTREE. Phase commits are built onto a per-batch ref by plumbing (`git commit-tree` plus compare-and-swap `git update-ref`, the idiom context/patterns/ref-plumbing-landing.md already documents and milestone-ref-land.sh already implements), never by checkout, so the primary tree never changes branch and R1-amended holds. The task's own range is then readable and the squash is a real pick. Cost: every phase commit goes through plumbing rather than ordinary commit, which touches the commit scripts the held two-root tasks also touch.

B. NO SQUASH; LANDING DEGRADES TO VERIFICATION. Phase commits stay on the integration branch as made. "Landing" becomes the pre-completion check that the task's work is present at the tip, plus the review handoff. The reviewable unit is the phase sequence, not one commit. Cost: gives up one-commit-per-task, which R3-amended asserts; the record must be amended, not quietly departed from.

C. SQUASH AT REVIEW TIME, NOT LANDING TIME. Phase commits stay as made; the squash happens when the review branch is cut or when the forge merges. Cost: pushes the unit-of-review decision into the PR task that depends on this one; state the interface explicitly if chosen.

A history rewrite of the integration branch is NOT a candidate: guard-destructive-git.sh refuses a HEAD-moving reset while another writer is live, and `git rebase -i` is unavailable.

=== WHAT THE TASK BUILDS ONCE RULED ===

1. LANDING at a task's [IMPLEMENTING] -> [COMPLETED] transition in orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, under the existing specs/.commit-lock mutex, in the PRIMARY tree, which never changes branch. Subject `task {N}: {title}`, body carrying the session identity and the phase list. `git merge --squash` of an end commit is rejected by the record: it co-lands a sibling's unfinished commits when tasks interleave. Do not rely on `modified_files` to find the work; read the refs.
2. REFUSAL, never a skip: a commit in the range attributable to no task, or a pick conflict, refuses the landing, leaves the task un-completed and the refs intact, and names the offending commit.
3. VERIFICATION strictly BEFORE the completion status write: blob equality over the task's own path set, between the new integration tip and the task's end commit. Full-tree equality is the wrong predicate here. Ship a deliberate NEGATIVE fixture proving the check fails when work did not land, and record that it was observed failing. This item is the one that closes defect 4 (silent non-landing under a completed status) and it survives every option above -- build it whichever way the ruling goes.
4. IDEMPOTENT: a re-run after a recorded landing proof is a no-op. Record the proof in the batch record that the admission task registers; cleanup depends on it.
5. TWO CONCURRENT BATCHES on one integration branch: the second landing can conflict. Build the conflict fixture; the response is refusal with the refs intact.
6. SOURCE-STORE COMMITS made by commit-source-store-path.sh in a second repository are outside the range and outside the squash. State them in the body or rule otherwise, with reasons.
7. RETIRE milestone-ref-land.sh as a landing mechanism and point milestone-review-handoff.sh's review range at the integration branch. Its `--verify` tree-equality predicate is weaker than item 3's blob equality; do not leave the repository with no pre-completion landing verification at any point in the transition.
8. INTERFACE TO PR SUBMISSION: whatever the ruling, state in the decision record what a downstream PR-cutting step receives -- the ref it branches from, the commit range it covers, and whether that range is already one commit per task. The PR and stacking task depends on this contract and must not have to re-derive it.

DEFERRED WITH THE WORKTREE TASKS: the back-merge of the integration branch into a batch branch after each landing, which exists only to fix a batch branch's merge base. Reinstate it when isolation returns.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS: (1) repo-agnostic -- no literal branch name and no consumer-repo path in any deliverable; (2) add NO prose to skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md or commands/orchestrate.md, both at their byte ceilings; (3) git push and PR/MR creation stay prohibited for agents, guard-destructive-git.sh is respected, and git rebase -i is unavailable.

VERIFICATION CRITERIA THIS TASK OWNS:
- The contradiction above is ruled in a decision record under specs/decisions/ before any code lands, and the ruling names which of the record's assertions it amends.
- A multi-task batch produces one reviewable unit per completed task on the integration branch, with its phase list recorded, the primary tree never having changed branch.
- A task failing mid-batch leaves its commits and refs intact while its sibling lands.
- A completion status write cannot occur without the landing verification having passed, demonstrated by a negative fixture observed failing.

1. guard-destructive-git.sh evaluates the tree the command TARGETS. This is the most likely failure in practice: an agent's working directory resets to the project directory on every Bash call and every relative path resolves there.

A payload path inside an external worktree is outside the project directory; each hook must either handle it or refuse loudly, never pass silently. Deployed settings reference $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in hook commands, so hooks resolve the primary tree whatever the worktree contains.

Depends on the harness measurement: what working directory and payload path a hook actually receives for a worktree file is measured there, not assumed here.

### 665. Record the last dispatching orchestration batch in a displaced Previous work section of the generated roadmap
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: orchestrator
- **Dependencies**: Task 697

**Description**: Record the last dispatching orchestration batch in a displaced "Previous work" section of the generated roadmap

GOAL (user's own words): "when I orchestrate a task, that task shows up under a 'Previous work', but only one orchestration batch should be listed, where it is displaced each time."

Exactly ONE record is retained at any time: the most recent DISPATCHING /orchestrate invocation's batch. Each new dispatching invocation overwrites (displaces) it. Never an append-only history, never a growing list, never two batches at once.

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** in /home/benjamin/.config/nvim (resolved via .claude-extensions.json's .extensions.core.source_dir). Never hand-author under the deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit the source-store path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh.

=== SETTLED BY THE REQUESTING OPERATOR -- NOT RE-OPENABLE ===

R1. ONLY A DISPATCHING INVOCATION DISPLACES THE RECORD. An invocation that dispatched nothing leaves the existing record standing, untouched. The section means "the last batch that actually did work", not "the last command I typed". The operator was shown the alternative (every invocation displaces, with a "not dispatched" outcome rendered) and declined it explicitly. Do not re-litigate this; design to it.

   The mechanical predicate is already available at the write site and must be used rather than re-derived: the invocation's multi-state file carries .dispatch_start_ts, a per-task map that is EMPTY exactly when no dispatch was issued. This is the same signal the existing Move 4 finalize sequence already reads to compute forward_progress_violated. A non-empty .dispatch_start_ts is the ruled definition of "dispatching"; an empty one means skip the write entirely and leave the prior record intact.

R2. PLACEMENT: the section renders immediately AFTER the milestone summary table and BEFORE the first milestone section, as a top-level "## Previous work" heading. The operator chose this over a trailing position beside "Open tasks in no batch", on the grounds that "what just happened" should read before "what is planned". The existing reading order is otherwise unchanged: sentinel, "# Roadmap", primary-goals bullets, milestone summary table, [NEW SECTION], "See also" link, milestone sections, "Rules, conventions and repo context", "Open tasks in no batch". Resolve where the "See also" link sits relative to the new section as a presentation detail, but the section itself goes between the table and the first milestone.

=== MEASURED EVIDENCE -- RE-DERIVABLE, DO NOT RE-DERIVE FROM SCRATCH ===

M1. THE GENERATED ROADMAP IS A PURE FUNCTION OF state.json. scripts/roadmap-integration.sh computes the entire file in one jq pass held in the MS_RENDER_JQ shell variable, reading exactly four input families: .primary_goals (falling back to .active_goal), .roadmap_milestones[], .roadmap_context, and .active_projects[] plus the sibling archive at $(dirname STATE_PATH)/archive/state.json. It reads NOTHING from specs/events.jsonl, specs/.orchestration/, or git history. The new section must therefore be fed from a state.json key written ahead of the render, never derived at render time from an orchestration log.

M2. THE RENDERED SECTION INVENTORY is small and fully enumerated by MS_RENDER_JQ's final emission block: the generated sentinel, "# Roadmap", the primary-goals bullet list, the milestone summary table, a "See also" link, one msection() per milestone (each containing bsection() per batch), an anchored "## Rules, conventions and repo context" holding listsec() subsections for Repository/Rules/Conventions, and a trailing "### Open tasks in no batch" fenced block. The new section slots into that emission block at the position R2 fixes.

M3. THE RENDERER SPEAKS A LINE PROTOCOL, not direct printf. MS_RENDER_JQ emits L/BS/O/X/BE records consumed by render_milestone_file()'s while-read dispatcher: L prints a literal line; BS opens a row buffer; O emits an open task whose status token is resolved by status_token/token_rank from the task's own JSON; X emits a done or missing task with a caller-supplied token; BE flushes the buffer sorted by token rank then task number, through format_task_row. Reuse this protocol rather than inventing a second row formatter.

   THE CENTRAL RENDERING PROBLEM: the existing O and X vocabulary reports a task's CURRENT status, not what a given invocation DID to it. The new section needs a per-invocation outcome. X already accepts a caller-supplied token (it is how "done" and "missing" are emitted today), so it is the closer fit -- but confirm that token_rank's sort order and format_task_row's column widths behave sensibly for whatever outcome vocabulary is chosen, and extend them deliberately rather than by accident.

M4. THE ONCE-PER-INVOCATION WRITE SITE ALREADY EXISTS. scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh is invoked unconditionally from skill-orchestrate's Move 4 finalize sequence, documented in context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md Step 5 as the SOLE executor -- never called from Move 5's body and never twice per invocation. It already receives --session SID and --state-file pointing at the invocation's multi-state file, which carries .task_numbers, .completed_tasks, .failed_tasks, .current_statuses, .dispatch_start_ts and .cycle_count. It already resolves the output path, classifies it via lib/roadmap-preflight-lib.sh classify, and on a `generated` verdict calls roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate followed by a scoped commit of that path alone. It is the correct site to land the displaced record BEFORE the regenerate it already performs, so one pass and one commit carry both.

M5. THE MOTIVATING OBSERVATION. An orchestration invocation regenerated the roadmap and committed it, but the diff was a single unrelated line -- a newly created task appearing in "Open tasks in no batch" -- because the invocation dispatched nothing: the planner returned a no_eligible_stuck stop verdict at admission, three declared predecessors being unfinished and out of batch. Nothing in the file recorded that an orchestration had happened at all. Under R1 that specific run correctly writes no record; the gap it exposed is that a SUCCEEDING run leaves no trace either, which is what this work closes.

=== WHAT TO BUILD ===

A. STATE SCHEMA: one new state.json key holding exactly one record. The record needs at minimum the invocation's task numbers, each task's per-invocation outcome, each task's title (see D below), the session identity, and a timestamp. Decide and document whether it sits as a new top-level key beside roadmap_milestones/roadmap_context, or nested inside roadmap_context -- noting that roadmap_context currently holds only the three prose listsec families (overview/rules/conventions), so nesting an outcome record there may be a category error. Add the schema row to whichever declaration document owns the roadmap state surface, beside the existing roadmap_milestones/roadmap_context rows.

B. WRITER in scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh: compose the record from the multi-state file the script already reads and land it via state-write.sh -- never a hand-rolled jq-to-tmp-and-mv rewrite of state.json, which that script exists to own. Observe CLAUDE.md's jq-command-safety rule (use select(.x == "y" | not), never the != form, which gets escaped and breaks). The write must land BEFORE the --regenerate call in the same invocation so the regenerate already performs renders the new record in the same pass and the same commit. Displacement is a REPLACE of the single record, never an append. Gate the whole write on R1's .dispatch_start_ts predicate.

C. RENDERER in scripts/roadmap-integration.sh's MS_RENDER_JQ plus render_milestone_file: emit the new section from the state key, at R2's position, reusing the L/BS/O/X/BE protocol and format_task_row per M3. An absent or empty record renders NO section at all -- not an empty heading, not a placeholder -- so a store that has never had a dispatching invocation produces the file it produces today.

D. OUTCOME AND TITLE CARRYING: the record stores each task's title alongside its number, rather than resolving titles at render time from active_projects. Two reasons, both load-bearing: a completed task migrates out of active_projects into the archive and would otherwise lose its title or force the renderer to widen what it reads; and a vault operation renumbers tasks, after which a stored bare number is meaningless while a stored title still reads. State explicitly in the format doc that these titles are a point-in-time snapshot and intentionally do not track later retitling.

=== DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RULE ON DURING PLANNING (do not silently default) ===

Q1. Does the record still get written when the roadmap preflight verdict is NOT `generated` (absent, classic, stage, unknown), where orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh skips the regenerate entirely and degrades loudly at three surfaces? State-writing and file-rendering are independent concerns, and a skipped render is not obviously a reason to lose the state record -- but a record written into a store whose roadmap is hand-authored will surface only at some later migration. Rule explicitly either way and document the ruling.

Q2. What outcome does the record show for a dispatching invocation whose task ended in a non-terminal exception state ([PARTIAL], [BLOCKED]) versus completed versus failed? The multi-state file distinguishes .completed_tasks from .failed_tasks, but a task that was dispatched and ended [PARTIAL] or [BLOCKED] appears in NEITHER array, so the outcome vocabulary cannot be derived from those two arrays alone -- .current_statuses is the third input that closes the gap. Fix the full vocabulary and its render order.

Q3. Does a run that dispatched some tasks and refused others record only the dispatched ones, or the whole invocation roster with the refused ones marked? R1 governs whether the RECORD IS WRITTEN AT ALL (any dispatch means it is); it does not settle the record's MEMBERSHIP once written. Rule explicitly.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

- Repo-agnostic: no consumer-repo-specific path or literal in any deliverable.
- Additive. Must not change the existing rendered sections' content or relative order beyond inserting the new section at R2's position, and must not alter what the roadmap commit stages (the scoped commit of the resolved output path alone).
- The regenerate must stay a pure function of state.json (M1). Do not make the renderer read events.jsonl, specs/.orchestration/, or git.
- Regenerating twice from unchanged state must stay byte-identical. The record carries a timestamp, so the timestamp must come from the WRITE, never from render time, or idempotence breaks.
- The generator refuses to overwrite a non-generated file (refuse_non_generated, a permanent property per roadmap-format.md). Do not weaken that refusal.
- Do not edit the roadmap generator's caller contract (context/patterns/roadmap-update.md) in a way that changes an existing caller's mode; this work adds a write to one caller, it does not re-wire the caller split. Note that postflight-tool-restrictions.md's Conclusion Stage table names that contract as invoked-never-edited from the stage body; this task edits the generator and its own documented caller script, which is a different actor from the stage body, so confirm the boundary reading during planning.
- No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md). Note the tension this creates with A, C and D: the RECORD's own payload legitimately contains task numbers as DATA, in state.json and in the rendered roadmap under specs/**, which is the primary exemption zone for both rules -- but the prose of any script comment, doc or test under agent-system/** must not cite a task number.
- git push and pull-request creation stay prohibited for agents (rules/pr-prohibition.md).

=== VERIFICATION ===

A dispatching /orchestrate invocation that completes a task leaves exactly one "Previous work" record naming that task, its title and its outcome, rendered between the milestone summary table and the first milestone section. A second dispatching invocation on a different task REPLACES that record entirely: the first invocation's tasks are gone from the file and the section never holds two batches. An invocation refused at admission with zero dispatches writes nothing and leaves the prior record byte-identical -- verified against the real signal, an empty .dispatch_start_ts. A store with no record renders no section and no empty heading. Regenerating twice from unchanged state is byte-identical. The generator still refuses to overwrite a non-generated file. Every pre-existing section renders unchanged apart from the insertion. Both named test scripts cover the new section, the displacement, the zero-dispatch no-write path, and the absent-record no-section path.
